summary: Extracts the HIGH-5 bounded-join pattern from NativeProbeBackend::stop_probe into a pub(crate) fn bounded_join_with_timeout(handle, timeout) -> BoundedJoinResult, so the timeout branch (the reason the guard exists) becomes testable without paying its 10s cost. stop_probe keeps calling it with Duration::from_secs(10) and emits the same three log lines. Two unit tests prove the contract in 0.10s: fast thread -> Joined, 10s sleeper + 100ms budget -> Timeout within 250ms. Closes the deferral from m9-62 (repeated in m9-67/m9-68 release-reports).
title: 69 bounded join unit test

subject.gap: m9-62 added stop_probe's bounded join (spawn a waiter that joins the probe thread, then recv_timeout on the caller's stack) to prevent a wedged probe thread from deadlocking the MCP response path. The timeout branch is the whole reason the guard exists, but the 10s timeout was hardcoded, so no test exercised it: m9-62, m9-67, and m9-68 all deferred the unit test as a '10s runtime blocker'.
subject.fix: Extracted the pattern into `pub(crate) fn bounded_join_with_timeout(handle: JoinHandle<()>, timeout: Duration) -> BoundedJoinResult` (Joined/Timeout/Panicked). stop_probe calls it with Duration::from_secs(10); the three results map onto the same log lines as before. Added `bounded_join_returns_joined_when_thread_exits_quickly` and `bounded_join_returns_timeout_when_thread_overruns` (10s sleeper + 100ms budget, asserts return within 250ms). Both pass in 0.10s.
